main_text.l: gnoscit, atque etiam obligare: sed ob
illorum jurium plerumque incertitudi-
nem, merito dubitari potest, quate-
nus obligent. Dicendum est, obligari
subditum indubie ad confervandum
quantum in ipso est omnia jura quae
νόμῳ aut ἔθῳ[?], legibus aut moribus
constat esse legitima; id est quae
aut jure scripto definita sunt, aut longo
temporis usu & diuturna (ut vocant)
præscriptione invaluerunt: quatenus sc.
ii nota sunt, vel etiam posthac moraliter
innotescere poterint. Non tamen pariter
obligari ad omnia ea observanda quae
sunt dubii aut controversi juris: præser-
tim cum soleant fere vi potestate præ-
diti funiculos agrorum extendere,
& ultra lapides clientium salire, nec
jurium suorum finibus contenti esse. De-
bet tamen subditus animo esse semper
parato, & illa quae sunt dubia, ubi justa
esse constiterit, agnoscere & tueri.
SECT. XVIII.
Ultimus Casus est, ubi exigitur Ju-
ramentum a membro alicujus commu-
nitatis, puta Civitatis, Academiæ, Col-
legii, aut societatis Mercatorum vel Ar-
tificum,

page.notes: The left margin is clipped by the scan edge: the first letters of several lines (e.g. "gnoscit", "illorum", "nem", "jurium") are partly cut off; they were read from the visible remainder and the reconstruction is as printed. Greek "νόμῳ" and the second Greek word ("ἔθῳ") are read from a small, faint print; the second Greek word is doubtful. "ui" was printed for the ablative "vi" and is corrected to "vi" under the u/v rule. The last line "tificum," is the end of "Artificum," split at the line end. The marginal note "Casus 16" is in the right margin beside "Ultimus Casus". Show-through and the "§9" page marker are otherwise left as seen.
